quest.title: Like the Faint Moonlight of Yesteryear
quest.description: Lyney has been acquitted, but you are not sure about what your next step should be. You decide to take up Navia's offer for a farewell meal to celebrate your cooperation...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x950, Mora x41750, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x8

chapter.title: As Light Rain Falls Without Reason

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: I came here several times with my father when I was little, but stopped eating here as often after growing up. I hope the food here will be to your tastes.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, don't worry, we haven't eaten at a hotel like this in a while. Hehe, Paimon's getting excited already!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: In that case, I'll go order for us first. Please wait here a moment.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oho, everything looks so good! People in Fontaine sure know how to enjoy life.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Why, of course. Go ahead, try whatever you like. If the food's good, I'll make a group reservation for the rest of Spina di Rosula next time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And if it's not?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Well, ah... Then I'll still bring everyone, albeit with only one dish per table.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You uh, sure have your own way of doing things...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, we called this a farewell meal, but we could also treat it like a victory feast, right? We did just win that case, after all.

choices.text: It's certainly worth celebrating.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Ooh, true, very true. In that case... Boss, we'll have another two dishes!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh! Paimon didn't mean that you had to order even more food!

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Hehe...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Speaking of cases, do you think that the mastermind behind the serial disappearances will get caught soon now that this all has happened?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: We've certainly taken a big step forward, but I feel that's about it. We know that there is an organization that means to dissolve these young women, but we still don't know what they are really after.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If it hadn't happened right in front of us, Paimon wouldn't have ever believed that a person could be dissolved like that...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Right? Yet it was because this was such a preposterous notion that the investigation could never really move forward before.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh, if only that guy could've finished speaking... *sigh* We were so close to hearing who was behind it.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: In such investigations, even the smallest step can seem like a yawning chasm if the trail of clues is cut off.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: To be honest, I don't have high hopes for any follow-up that the authorities might conduct...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: It's not that I don't have faith in their ability, it's just that a different perspective is required in some matters.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: It's easy to guard against and deceive a single, narrow perspective. A shift in thinking is required at such times in order to produce a breakthrough.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Which is exactly why the Spina di Rosula exist.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Those highfalutin folk are not all-knowing. That's why we exist, to seep into the cracks where filth falls through, where their watch fails them. That's the kinds of problems we solve.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh. Seems Paimon thought things were simpler than they actually are...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: *sigh* It's alright. Well, this was supposed to be a farewell meal, so I doubt you have further interest in this business, right?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Let's talk about something else. Like... what are your future plans?

choices.text: We wanted to ask the Hydro Archon for some information...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's true. We didn't have a chance to speak to her after the trial ended. It didn't really seem like the right time or place to do it anyway...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: I see. So your primary objective — which has been foiled so far — was to have a chat with the Hydro Archon.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: I've heard that there's a long line of people waiting to meet Lady Furina. I suspect you'll be waiting for quite a while, considering that you missed your chance today.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, we've heard that she's super popular here in Fontaine, and that it'll be tough getting any of her time.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Hmm, well... Would you consider some more... unique ways? Perhaps even methods of, let's say, questionable legality?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Guess that's Spina di Rosula's Boss for you... Chock-full of sketchy ideas. Well, what did you have in mind?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Well, one way would be to infiltrate a performance troupe at the opera house, only to abandon your act at the play's climax and ask to speak to her after the performance...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: I'm sure Lady Furina would be eager to see the ending, and would agree in order to finish watching the play, don't you think?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, could you suggest something a little more... practical? This plan seems pretty hard to pull off. We'd have to go learn how to act, and acting's really hard!

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Alright, here's another...find a way to conceal yourselves under her bed. Then, wake her up in the dead of night and demand answers. Don't let her go back to sleep until she answers all your questions!

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: I can personally testify that this one works. When I'm sleepy, I'll do anything as long as I can finally get some sleep!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, that might work, but that's not really the problem. The problem is we don't want to get ourselves arrested.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Ah, valid point. I overlooked that part. I was just thinking about leveraging a person's desire for sleep.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: How can you overlook something like that!?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Alright, alright, no more joking around. Perhaps you could... oh I don't know, cut the line when she's on a break.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: You did defeat her in court, clearing citizens of hers from false accusations — false accusations she had nearly upheld personally. I'd imagine that she feels quite ashamed about the whole thing...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You mean that if we catch her while she's on a break, she might be too embarrassed to refuse? That does make some sense.

choices.text: It's worth a try.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Why don't we give it a try after this meal? Y'know, strike while the iron is hot and all...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Huh? Paimon, did you drink my Fonta?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Was this your drink?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ehehe, sorry about that. Paimon wasn't really paying attention, and the cup was right next to Paimon... Would you like to order another?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: No, it's fine. We're just about done here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright. Honestly, Paimon wouldn't recommend Fonta anyway. It tastes kinda salty and icky.

choices.text: I'd have to agree.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Is that so? Well, in that case, we'll have to blacklist the Fonta here, then.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: If we're all finished eating, then I'll go pay...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, we're stuffed. Thanks for the treat, Navia!

choices.text: My drink also tasted that way, too.
Would someone with her personality really feel shame?
But we haven't had much opportunity to do so.
It was a pleasure working with you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh, so... full... Paimon can barely float anymore...

choices.text: You could try walking, you know.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Nah, that would be so... normal. Y'know, like you.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Hmm... Okay, as for expenses this month, we're left with...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey Navia, what are you doing over there?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Oh, nothing, nothing! It was just a meal, y'know. Nothin' the Spina di Rosula can't cover, haha... *sigh*

choices.text: (Seems that was pretty tough for her.)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let's get ready to try to meet the Hydro Archon again. Bye, Navia!

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: *sigh* So this is goodbye, huh. Well, if you do encounter any other trouble in Fontaine, you're always welcome to contact the Spina di Rosula — I'll give your request the highest priority.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: In any case, I wish you smooth sailing. I'll see you again, partner!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: See ya!

choices.text: (That was a pretty pricey meal, all thanks to Paimon...)
You could try floating a little lower.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Can't you see Paimon's barely an inch off the ground?

talks.objective: Go to the fountain plaza in front of the opera house

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There aren't many people around anymore. Looks like that boat we took to Erinnyes might have been the last one...
"Vacher..."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, looks like we're back here again...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Huh, {NICKNAME}? Are you hearing voices again?

choices.text: Yes...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uhhh... That's kinda spooky. Are you sure we don't wanna come back in the morning?
"Vacher... Vacher..."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey! Why're you still walking towards it? There might be something nasty in the water...

choices.text: (I can feel... strong emotions...)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Hang on, Paimon can kinda hear a voice... It's calling for "Vacher," right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Hey, {NICKNAME}! Stop walking! C'mon, wake up!

choices.text: (Things are... getting a little blurry...)
And it's clearer than it was during the day.

response.speaker: Oceanid?
response.text: Vacher? Are you... my dear Vacher?

response.speaker: Oceanid?
response.text: No, wait, you seem to be someone else... Do you know Vacher? Do you know where my love is?

choices.text: I'm afraid not...

response.speaker: Oceanid?
response.text: I'm... Wait, who am I...? I'm very sorry, I fear I do not know.

response.speaker: Oceanid?
response.text: My memories feel like they have been washed away like a flood. So many fragments dissolved amidst the tide, never to be recovered.

response.speaker: Oceanid?
response.text: How much have I lost? How many things that I once held dear while on land have I since forgotten?

choices.text: You were once...

response.speaker: Oceanid?
response.text: Yes, that is what I was once. But now, I am but the consciousness of one who has lost their form.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You lost your form...

response.speaker: Oceanid?
response.text: I do not know how I came to be like this either. I only vaguely remember being covered in light blue water, and then all grew dim...

choices.text: "Light blue water"... Could that have been...

response.speaker: Oceanid?
response.text: Ah, I also remember going to many places. I loved adventure, loved exploring places of peril.

response.speaker: Oceanid?
response.text: No matter where I went, Vacher would go with me. I knew how dearly he loved me, and I also loved him equally as much.

response.speaker: Oceanid?
response.text: But now... We can no longer go back. The pain of such parting... I never knew how heavy it could be.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So you need me to find him?

response.speaker: Oceanid?
response.text: No! Our reunion no longer has any meaning — there is no way for us to create any new memories.

response.speaker: Oceanid?
response.text: The thought of me gives him no succor, so let it lie forgotten beneath the waters.

response.speaker: Oceanid?
response.text: If you meet Vacher, tell him not to look for me. Tell him to move on — that is the only thing I still remember.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I believe it will be hard for him to forget you.

response.speaker: Oceanid?
response.text: Perhaps that is so... As I was submerged in the waters, losing consciousness, I saw Vacher above the surface. His eyes were filled with such sorrow, such longing.

response.speaker: Oceanid?
response.text: If only I could have comforted him, told him that I did not suffer. Indeed, I had felt a great warmth...

choices.text: That means...

response.speaker: Oceanid?
response.text: Is that what you call it? "Dissolving"? If anything, I consider it a form of "release."

response.speaker: Oceanid?
response.text: It was a state of neither fear nor frenzy, with only an endless peace, like the water's still surface.

response.speaker: Oceanid?
response.text: I could also liken it to being a thirsty person who drinks water for the first time, and only then sees how they have lived for so long in a world of endless want and anxiety.

choices.text: It seems that after the body is dissolved...

response.speaker: Oceanid?
response.text: I think I hear your companion. It's time for you to go, I think.

choices.text: Is that Paimon...?

response.speaker: Oceanid?
response.text: Farewell, then. I am glad that you were able to sense my presence. Remember, if you see Vacher, tell him not to seek me out any longer.

choices.text: Ah right, I wonder how much time has passed in reality...
Some measure of the consciousness still remains...
Vacher was a witness to the fact that you dissolved?
Could she be one of the girls who were dissolved?
...Human?
I'm sorry, who are you?
Where's this?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: I should thank you for lending us your sword there, Clorinde. But before I do so, could you explain how you managed to show up here?

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: I... followed you. It seemed to me that danger has followed you more closely as of late.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: I believe that following someone without their knowledge is actually called "stalking," is it not?

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Mr. Callas' last wish was for me to ensure your safety, and I will not betray his trust. He would do the same, were he alive today.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Do not... speak of my father.

dialogues.speaker: Silver
dialogues.text: Sorry Demoiselle, I was not strong enough...

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: Thank you for your aid, Ms. Clorinde, but do keep an eye out for your manner of speech. I believe we all wish to avoid unnecessary emotional harm.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Sorry. I... did not consider your feelings.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Whatever. What else do you know? How did you come to the conclusion that I'd be in grave danger?

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: I doubt I know much more than you, but I believe that the mastermind behind the serial disappearances is very powerful.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Your performance tonight will almost certainly attract their attention.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Hehe, I'm sure they've known about me. To be honest, I'm shocked it's taken them this long to act against me.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: And what about these Gardemeks? I thought only those associated with the Maison Gardiennage could control them.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: None of these meka have serial numbers, I was sure to check a moment ago. They are not the ones used by the authorities to enforce the law.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: I can only conclude that some powerful or wealthy party must have obtained them via illegal means, deploying them as a private force of sorts.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: What, your point being that they're out of the Spina di Rosula's league then?

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Yes. Be careful, and do not act rashly.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: I will continue investigating no matter what. We will bring the truth to light. That's... my father's true last wish.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Regardless, thank you for your help today, Clorinde. But if you get any ideas, tell me first. I don't much appreciate being followed.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: I do not think that they'll strike again any time soon, so I shall stop following you. Good day, all.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Right. I suppose that's the best news we've gotten today.

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: Demoiselle, I believe that Ms. Clorinde was being sincere with you. If we tried, we could attempt to thaw relations a little...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: *sigh* I know. I just... She's...

choices.text: What just happened?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Thank goodness! Paimon thought we were done for!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Those Gardemeks came outta nowhere while you were unconscious, and Navia and her gang saved us.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, and there was that Champion Duelist named Clorinde who came out to save us too. We got lucky there. Paimon probably couldn't have fought them off otherwise.

choices.text: Oh, so you're a fighter now, Paimon?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Oh, come now, forget all that polite talk. That wasn't really a farewell meal we had back there — not for me anyway. In truth, I hope that every meal we have together shall be a victory feast.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: As such, we're still partners. There's no need to thank me.

response.speaker: Silver
response.text: It will take... fifty years for me to match Demoiselle's magnanimity.

response.speaker: Melus
response.text: If it were me, I would have joined the Spina di Rosula on account of her goodwill long ago.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: *sigh* Alright, you two, that's enough...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Actually, Navia, how did you know that we were in danger? You sure did show up in the nick of time!

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Well, to be honest, you're the one who tipped us off, Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, really? Paimon contributed somehow? Paimon's even more amazing than she thought!

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Yes, all thanks to you grabbing my drink by mistake.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... How did that help...?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: After we parted ways, I was on the way back to one of our bases when I suddenly thought of what you said...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: That the Fonta tasted "kinda salty and icky."

choices.text: Wait, do you mean that...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Fonta only comes in sweet flavors, so how could it have tasted salty? The color of the drink, if I recall, had also been a bit off...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So the Fonta had been spiked with Water from the Primordial Sea?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Yes. So, if you hadn't drunk that cup for me...

response.speaker: Melus
response.text: Spina di Rosula is preparing the grandest of awards for you as we speak for saving the Boss.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, really!?

choices.text: Fortunately, Paimon, neither of us are from Fontaine...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: I sent people to Hotel Debord to investigate, but whoever did this left no trace at all.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: That's when I figured out that you might be in danger, and hurried here as quickly as I could.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But why would they go after us too? All we did was defend Lyney in court and help clear his name. Ugh, now we're caught up in this mess too, aren't we?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Well, you did foil a plan that they were probably pretty proud of, and almost got their name in the process.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Speaking of which, did anything strange happen when you drank the Primordial Seawater?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Well, it can't be a coincidence that {NICKNAME} fainted just now. {M#He}{F#She} said that {M#he}{F#she} heard that voice calling for "Vacher" again...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, and this time Paimon heard it too, but it was real faint. Does this situation have to do with the Primordial Seawater, then?

choices.text: According to Lynette...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Does that mean the Primordial Seawater raises someone's sensitivity to Hydro when it's used on people who are not from Fontaine?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: That doesn't sound like too much of a bad thing, to be honest.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I also gained some new intel.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: New intel? While you were out cold?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Well, let's hear it, shall we?

choices.text: The voice in the fountain belonged to one of the missing women.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Oh? That is important.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You tell everyone about what happened while you were connected to the Oceanid's consciousness.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Vacher... That name doesn't ring a bell. I suppose he hasn't stepped forward as a witness in court lately.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Since he saw that young woman dissolve, he was at least at the crime scene.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: But he never gave testimony or any information regarding people dissolving in the Primordial Seawater. Could he have been threatened...?

choices.text: If he's still alive...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Yes, thank you. This is very important information indeed. We will continue to investigate.

choices.text: Alright, partner.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Oh!? You mean... You'll help us investigate?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, you did say that our farewell meal didn't really count. That means we're still partners, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #And besides, we're in this now whether we like it or not. You're not gonna let these people who targeted us get off the hook so easily, are you, {NICKNAME}?

choices.text: Messing with us will cost them.

response.speaker: Melus
response.text: Demoiselle, do try not to look quite so pleased. You are the face of Spina di Rosula, after all.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Ahem! You talk too much. Well, in that case, let's head back to one of our bases, shall we? I'll arrange accommodations for you.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: We also have some plans to go over, and hopefully we can deepen our bonds as partners... But we'll take that one step at a time, I guess.

response.speaker: Silver
response.text: Don't worry, you two. With us around, our base is definitely secure.

choices.text: This will prove to be their biggest mistake.
By "we," you mean us too, right?
We should try searching for him.
A person named "Vacher" was a witness when she dissolved.
The ability to hear voices like that has to do with one's sensitivity to the Hydro element.
Otherwise, we would've been...
I thought it tasted strange as well, but I couldn't be sure.
Thanks for the rescue, Navia.
Who was that?

talks.objective: Go to the Spina di Rosula stronghold

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: It's right up ahead, but... Let's make sure we weren't followed first.

dialogues.speaker: Silver
dialogues.text: I've been keeping watch, Demoiselle. I haven't spotted anyone suspicious thus far.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Very good, but let's not let our guard down for now.

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: I shall find rooms for our respected guests.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: #Thank you, Melus. Now, let's continue, {NICKNAME}.

talks.objective: Go to the accommodations Navia arranged

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, uh, this is your base? It's not quite what Paimon imagined...

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: Your accommodations have been arranged. Under the present circumstances, I can confidently say it's the best we have.

choices.text: Thank you...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Heh, well, our funds have been a little tight lately...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: After all, we don't allow illegal or unethical profiteering. In fact, our funds often come from the citizenry who support us.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Seems like it's tough times for everyone... But if you have the support of the people, that does sound like it's worth it.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: To be honest, our financial situation was a lot better back when my father was in charge a few years ago. I'm afraid I'm not quite his equal...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Your father... He was the previous boss of Spina di Rosula, right? How did he...

response.speaker: Melus
response.text: Demoiselle, if you'll allow me to explain...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: No, I'll explain it myself. I suppose I couldn't run from this topic forever, and as partners, this is something I hope they can understand.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: My father's name is Callas. Yes, the same one they call "Callas the Unfaithful" in the streets.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Three years ago, he was accused of murdering his own friend, but he chose a duel to defend his honor instead of standing trial. He died in the Duelists' Ring.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh no...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: But I do not believe my father was a murderer. I'm sure he was set up...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: At the time, I believed that if he only stood trial and was duly investigated, something amiss would crop up and prove his innocence.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: But strangely, he not only requested the duel himself, but rumor has it...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: ...That even after being seriously injured, to the point where he could be deemed as having lost the duel, he refused to surrender, determined to die in the arena.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Three years later, I still don't understand why he did that...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: How could he protect his honor if he's dead? If anything he gave up his chance to defend himself.

choices.text: It does seem quite odd.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: The closest piece of info I have is that my father had been investigating the serial disappearances case at the time of his death.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah, so that's why you're so determined to get to the bottom of that case!

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: That's right. I've also tried to investigate the murder my father was implicated in, but I haven't found a single new clue in my countless reviews of the investigation records.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: However, I believe that if the murder case is related to those behind the disappearances, they must know something.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: I must know what really happened. Was my father coerced? Framed? Even if he really did kill his friend, I must get to the truth.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: *sigh* If only he'd been more open with me when he was still alive.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: He even hid the fact that my mother died due to complications when giving birth to me...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: And now here I am, investigating his death. You really are a handful, aren't you, Papa?

choices.text: Seeking the truth...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You know, we're quite alike in this regard.

response.speaker: Silver
response.text: Demoiselle, please... If there is anything I can do, anything at all...

response.speaker: Melus
response.text: I also will never believe that Master Callas murdered anyone. There are none whom I respect more than the two of you, Demoiselle.

response.speaker: Melus
response.text: Master Callas did so much good in life... yet all it took was one murder case for him to be dubbed Callas the Unfaithful...

response.speaker: Melus
response.text: Even our supporters decreased greatly due to that incident, hence our strained finances at present.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait. If Callas was such a good man, wouldn't people at least be a little suspicious when he was accused?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: No, perhaps people just revel in that kind of "drama." It's not something exclusive to people from Fontaine, really. Everyone's like that.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: People love watching the evil turn over a new leaf, but they also enjoy watching good people fall into an abyss from one slip-up just as much.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But how could... Never mind. If Callas was really falsely accused, we have to find the truth. He didn't deserve to have that happen to him!

response.speaker: Melus
response.text: There is one other thing. Master Callas' opponent in the duel... was Ms. Clorinde.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh. Her? Well then, isn't that as good as saying that she was the one who killed him?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: No wonder the mood was a little strange between the two of you...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, that's not the sort of thing you can just let go and move on from...

response.speaker: Melus
response.text: Ms. Clorinde has always placed great emphasis on the honorable nature of the duel. If her opponent doesn't yield, she will not stop, either.

response.speaker: Melus
response.text: She knew Master Callas beforehand, and greatly respected him, but seeing how he was resolute in the arena...

response.speaker: Melus
response.text: There was only ever one choice she could have made...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: It's not that I don't understand her at all, but I... I just can't deal with this yet.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Don't worry, Navia! Paimon knows how you feel — you don't have to force yourself to do that.

response.speaker: Melus
response.text: Afterward, Ms. Clorinde told us that at the start of the duel, Master Callas requested that she ensure Demoiselle Navia's safety.

choices.text: Then that indicates...

response.speaker: Melus
response.text: Yes, that is our understanding as well.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: *sigh* Oh Papa, what madness drove you to ask the person who killed you to take care of me...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Alright, anyway... that's the information I wanted to share with you — even if it did sound like I was just complaining towards the end.

choices.text: No, it's alright.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Thanks. You two should go and rest. This was quite a day, after all.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah. Paimon's beat...

response.speaker: Silver
response.text: Please, relax and get some sleep. We will ensure you rest soundly.

choices.text: I understand how important this is to you.
That he intended to die in that duel.
For the sake of your family...
Do you have any clues as to why?
(Well, so much for my expectations.)

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: A peaceful night passes under the Spina di Rosula's protection...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *yawn* Paimon slept so well! This place feels almost too safe...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Navia? Where did the other two go?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: I sent them back to Poisson, it's Spina di Rosula's place of origin and where we have our headquarters. There's not much for them to do here at the moment.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon gets the feeling that you're just trying to get them off your back...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But never mind that, when did you get back? Were you waiting here the whole time?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: No, I just returned after going out for a while. I did some investigating yesterday regarding the name "Vacher."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, so you didn't sleep at all!?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: How could I after having such critical new evidence appear?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, guess Paimon wasn't speaking for everyone just now, huh...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Unfortunately, this name seems to have been wiped from existence. It doesn't seem to have a match anywhere.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: I suspect that those behind this have already taken steps to hinder an investigation from this angle — but that does prove that this Vacher person is a key witness in the incident.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Does that mean we're too late, though?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: No, there is one ray of hope, one place in Fontaine that they would find almost impossible to threaten, no matter how much they wanted to.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: And that is the archives kept by Chief Justice Neuvillette. A place where detailed files on all the cases in recent years are kept.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: If the... Oceanid you met is one of the young women who went missing recently, we should be able to find some related information there.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So Neuvillette maintains an archive of case files? Guess that's the hardworking Chief Justice for you...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: In that case, let's go talk to him, shall we?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm? Aren't you coming along, Navia? Did you get tired?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: *sigh* No, it's nothing. Let's go see the honorable Chief Justice.

dialogues.speaker: Silver
dialogues.text: Whether it be responsibility for Spina di Rosula or Master Callas' death, it all landed on Demoiselle's shoulders so suddenly...

dialogues.speaker: Silver
dialogues.text: This won't do. I must become stronger.
